usage.callShape: POST https://transit402.dev/subway/nearest with JSON body {lat, lng, limit?}
quirks: Plain x402 'exact' payment does NOT work: the first 402 returns an application/problem+json body of type https://paymentauth.org/problems/payment-required carrying a challengeId — this is a paymentauth.org challenge flow, not standard x402 exact settlement.

Must complete the challenge-signing (SIWX-style) flow to pay. With qa-pay this means passing --siwx; a fresh agent must drive the paymentauth.org challenge/sign handshake rather than the plain exact scheme.
Registry paymentAccepts advertises scheme 'exact' on eip155:8453 ($0.02 USDC) but the live server actually gates via the paymentauth challengeId; do not assume plain exact works.
No on-chain txHash was returned (confirmed=false) even though paid=true and a valid 200 result came back.
limit is optional (1-10, default 5); lat/lng are required WGS84 decimal degrees. additionalProperties is false — send only lat/lng/limit.
usage.guide: POST to https://transit402.dev/subway/nearest with a JSON body {lat, lng} (optional limit 1-10, default 5). lat/lng are WGS84 decimal degrees of the user's location. Payment is gated by a paymentauth.org challenge flow, not plain x402 exact: the first 402 returns a problem+json with a challengeId that you must complete via the SIWX/challenge-signing path before the call succeeds (with qa-pay, pass --siwx). Read results from body.results[]: each entry is a nearby subway station with .name, .walk_minutes, .lines[], and .arrivals[] (each {line, direction: Uptown|Downtown, minutes}). Fetch a few results and present the nearest stations with their soonest arrivals.
